segments.spoken: Before another return deadline slips past, let your AI help you check what is still eligible.
Agents like Muse, Instinct, and dots need your approved access.
Find recent purchases, check return policies, and list possible returns with deadlines and source links.
Have it include order and delivery dates, item condition, fees, and anything it cannot verify, because a receipt on its own may not establish whether a return is still eligible.
Sort the list by deadline, so a forgotten purchase does not disappear under another week of email.
Then choose the item numbers and ask for a return request draft. Make it show the next step before sending anything, cancelling anything, or accepting a charge.
For a pair of glasses, that means checking the exact policy, preparing the request, and showing you the next step. A return label depends on the retailer, and a request is not a refund.
You still need to check the details and send the item back. The useful part is cutting down all that admin.
For business software, audit upcoming renewals and check the contract before cancelling.
I’m Hammad. Save this prompt, and follow for practical AI workflows you can actually use.

resource_page.title: Check returns with AI
resource_page.body_markdown:
# AI return-check prompts

Review draft; not published.

## Find possible returns

Review the receipts I provide. List possible returns with item number, order and delivery dates, deadline, condition requirements, shipping/restocking fees, source policy links, and information you cannot verify. Sort by deadline. Do not submit or send anything.

## Prepare one request

For item [number], check the exact retailer policy and prepare a return-request draft. Show the proposed next action and any fees. Wait for my approval before sending, submitting, cancelling or accepting a charge.

A receipt alone may not establish eligibility. A request is not a refund. Account access, tools and regional availability vary. Use the actual merchant policy, not a generic return window.
